output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses is most likely caused by the 12 August relay server move, not by agency nurses. The new server imported only 3 of 14 forwarding rules. The skipped rules included the 15-second hold-off, repeat suppression and routing of technical alarms to the charge phone. The import tool logged a warning but reported success. Since then, phone notifications per nurse in Pods A-C have roughly doubled, and acknowledgement times have doubled. Pod D still uses the old server and shows no change, so it acts as a natural comparison. Within Pods A-C, core, agency and agency-like staff all deteriorated by similar amounts, and bedside alarm volume did not change. That counts against agency staffing, acuity and the monitor update as explanations. I did not test wireless coverage directly. The Pod D comparison makes it unlikely to be the main cause. The sick-leave rise may be linked to alarm overload, but that is unproven. Next steps: do not cap agency staff or open performance reviews. Restore the full forwarding rules (about 4 hours plus clinical validation), then track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Do not switch off SpO2 forwarding to phones.
